methodologyPage.title: Methodology
methodologyPage.intro: How ChainCompass gathers public network and market data and summarizes it for historical context.

about.title: What ChainCompass is and is not
about.body: ChainCompass presents historical network and market analysis for long-term context. It provides analysis only; it does not provide trading recommendations or forecasts and is not investment advice.

sources.title: Data and sources
sources.intro: Daily analytics use complete UTC days and are typically one day behind the current date. Provider delays can extend that interval. Missing dates remain gaps; values are not forward-filled or interpolated.
sources.tableCaption: Sources and their use in ChainCompass
sources.binance: Daily spot prices and quote-volume proxies for BTC, ETH, SOL, and BNB. Binance USDT close is used as a USD proxy.
sources.defillama: TVL, stablecoin supply, and DEX volume for ETH, SOL, and BNB. DEX analytics units are unverified; protocol fees are context only, not network fees.
sources.coinMetrics: Coin Metrics Community active-address and transaction metrics for BTC and ETH. Those SOL metrics are not available on the free tier; current BNB Chain entries are absent from its free catalog.
sources.coingecko: Market-cap snapshots for context and limited market-data fallback. Market-cap snapshots are not Health Score inputs.
sources.mempool: BTC network and RPC diagnostics. Its recommended fee rate is not a daily network-fee total.
sources.blockchain: BTC hashrate and daily transaction-fee totals. BTC fees in USD are derived using the same-day Binance BTC close.
sources.available: Available: a measured series is stored; this does not certify every value.
sources.unverified: Unverified: evidence is incomplete or a unit is not confirmed.
sources.notAvailable: Not available on free tiers: no suitable free series is confirmed.
sources.discontinued: Discontinued: the identified series ended and is not current chain coverage.
sources.notApplicable: Not applicable: the measure does not fit that network.
sources.derivedNote: Derived values and unverified units are labelled in the data views. BTC fees in USD are derived; DefiLlama DEX and protocol-fee units remain unverified.
sources.coverageNote: The free Coin Metrics tier does not provide current BNB Chain active-address or transaction metrics, or the requested SOL active-address, transaction, and fee metrics. BTC lacks available capital-pillar inputs; ETH lacks security-and-economics inputs; SOL and BNB lack adoption and security-and-economics inputs.

healthScore.title: Network Health Score
healthScore.intro: The score combines point-in-time, chain-relative component percentiles. Within each pillar, available component weights are re-normalized; pillar weights are also re-normalized over available pillars. Missing values are not imputed.
healthScore.percentile: Each component is ranked against its own trailing 1,095-day window, including the current date. At least 365 observations are required. The mid-rank percentile is used; lower-is-better components reverse the percentile.
healthScore.coverageMaximumIntro: Coverage is available component weight divided by 100. Maximum coverage is chain-specific:
healthScore.confidenceMedium: Medium confidence: coverage at least {value} and below the High threshold.
healthScore.confidenceLow: Low confidence: coverage below the Medium threshold.
healthScore.minimumCoverage: No score row is created below {value} coverage. Only ETH can reach High confidence because its maximum coverage is 0.90; BTC, SOL, and BNB max out below 0.80.
healthScore.partial: The Partial badge means the current score has less than that chain's maximum registered coverage. This field identifies the most recent date with full chain-specific coverage; it is a reference date, not the current score or current data time.
healthScore.fallbackNote: The methodology endpoint could not be reached. The table shows the documented v1 fallback values.

regimes.title: Regimes and risk flags
regimes.intro: Raw regime rules use fixed price-derived conditions in this priority order:
regimes.range: All other cases, including missing trend inputs
regimes.hysteresis: The first raw label initializes immediately. Later changes require the new raw label on five consecutive calendar dates. This five-day hysteresis makes the reported label lag a raw condition by design; gaps reset the consecutive-day count.
regimes.volatility: The <state>vol_state</state> overlay uses the percentile rank of <metric>realized_vol_90d</metric>: <high>high</high> at 80 or above, <low>low</low> at 20 or below, and <normal>normal</normal> between those thresholds. It is unavailable until its percentile can be calculated.

scenarios.title: Historical scenarios
scenarios.intro: Scenarios summarize historical realized returns over 30-, 90-, and 365-day horizons. The expanding sample uses <method>Hyndman-Fan type 7</method> quantiles: <quantiles>p10, p50, and p90</quantiles>.
scenarios.sample: The expanding history retains earlier market eras, including the 2017-2021 growth era; those periods can differ from current conditions.
scenarios.independence: <count>n_independent</count> is the number of exact-date return windows divided by the horizon in days. A horizon is available from five independent windows; <lowSample>low_sample</lowSample> marks 5-9, while 10 or more is the normal-sample range.
scenarios.note: Historical return quantiles, not a forecast.

research.title: Research findings
research.intro: The preregistered historical checks are descriptive, small-sample comparisons across a few market regimes.
research.shortHorizon: Pooled non-overlapping 30-day <band>p10-p90</band> hit rates were about <rate>0.87-0.90</rate> across the four chains, above the nominal 0.80 rate.
research.longHorizon: The 365-day horizons had 0-3 independent origins per chain, so calibration cannot be assessed reliably at that horizon.
research.scoreAssociation: Across 8 tests, the Health Score showed no association with forward returns distinguishable from zero; samples were small. Score inputs include price-derived market-condition components, so any relationship may reflect mechanical momentum or mean reversion rather than on-chain information.
research.regimes: Regime v2 was compared but not adopted; it produced more switching in the stored history.

limitations.title: Limitations
limitations.coverage: Some networks have no available free-tier on-chain inputs for particular pillars, and the score uses different component sets by chain.
limitations.history: Price and score histories start on different dates, and the longest scenario horizon has very few independent origins.
limitations.providers: Free-source coverage, units, and endpoints can change or become unavailable. Source gaps remain visible and are not filled.
limitations.scope: These pages describe the current analysis only. They do not establish future accuracy or outcomes.

assistant.title: The assistant
assistant.body: The assistant calls read-only tools over the same data services as the public analysis API and cannot change them. Each number in an answer is checked against results returned by those tools. Refusals are deterministic. It can still make mistakes; this check does not rule out every error. No evaluation with a live model has been run yet.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: The account service stores the following information for sign-in, account security, and essential account messages.
privacy.email: Account email, locale, email-verification state, account status, and account timestamps.
privacy.emailPurpose: Identify the account, select the language for account messages, and record verification and account status.
privacy.password: An Argon2id password hash for password-based accounts; the raw password is not stored. The hash can be empty for an account created through a configured external identity flow.
privacy.passwordPurpose: Verify a password without keeping the original password.
privacy.role: Account role, failed sign-in count, temporary lock time, and last sign-in time.
privacy.rolePurpose: Apply access controls and protect sign-in from repeated failures.
privacy.refresh: A SHA-256 hash of each refresh token, its family, expiry, revocation and replacement links, creation time, and the session user-agent and IP recorded by the server.
privacy.refreshPurpose: Rotate sessions, detect token reuse, and revoke sessions.
privacy.emailTokens: SHA-256 hashes of email-verification and password-reset tokens, with purpose, expiry, creation time, and use time.
privacy.emailTokensPurpose: Support one-time, expiring email verification and password-reset flows.
privacy.external: Provider account ID and email fields are supported by the account schema for external identity flows. Google sign-in is not available yet in the current product scope.
privacy.externalPurpose: Associate a configured external identity with an account.
privacy.conversations: Conversation records—including titles, your messages, tool results, and assistant answers—are stored in your account until you delete them. Deleting a conversation removes its messages and title.
privacy.usage: The service logs usage metadata: provider, model, prompt and completion token counts when available, response latency, status, time, and account and conversation references. These usage records do not contain message content.
privacy.aiProvider: When an AI provider is configured, the current message, recent conversation text, and tool results are sent to that provider to produce a response. The request does not include your email address, account ID, or account-level role. The configured provider's own terms and privacy practices apply.
privacy.publicData: Public market and network data requests carry no account identifiers; those requests are separate from AI-provider requests.

cookies.title: Cookies and browser storage
cookies.intro: These cookies and browser preferences support sign-in, language selection, or interface settings; they are essential to those functions.
cookies.refreshPurpose: Refreshes the short-lived in-memory access session. HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, scoped to /api/v1/auth; Secure follows deployment configuration.
cookies.csrfPurpose: Read by the client and echoed in a request header for CSRF checks. SameSite=Lax; not HttpOnly.
cookies.localePurpose: Remembers the selected language. SameSite=Lax, with a one-year lifetime.
cookies.oauthPurpose: Short-lived HttpOnly state for the Google callback when that flow is configured.
cookies.themePurpose: The selected light or dark appearance.
cookies.sidebarPurpose: Whether the application sidebar is collapsed.
cookies.logoutPurpose: A timestamp used only to notify another tab about sign-out when BroadcastChannel is unavailable.
cookies.accessToken: The short-lived access token is held in JavaScript memory only; it is not written to local storage. No analytics or advertising scripts are configured in the frontend.

sources.title: Data sources and attribution
sources.body: Public market and network data requests carry no account identifiers. This is separate from AI-provider requests described in the Privacy section. Coin Metrics Community data is for non-commercial use and requires attribution. Other data providers are credited in the methodology and subject to their own terms.
sources.emailProvider: In development, account email is saved to a local development mailbox. In other deployments, the configured SMTP service receives the recipient address and verification or password-reset message.
sources.accountDeletion: Account deletion controls are not available yet. Do not post passwords, account addresses, or authentication links in a public issue.
sources.contact: For questions about these terms or this privacy notice, use the public repository issues page.
